e: AWS DataSync transfers large datasets to FSx for Windows File Server quickly with parallel, optimized transfers, and it lets you set a bandwidth limit to protect the shared link. 30 TB in 5 days over a throttled shared 1 Gbps link is feasible. Snowcone is too small, and File Gateway and Transfer Family aren't bulk migration tools with bandwidth control.

Amazon Elastic Transcoder converts the raw videos into smaller formats suitable for mobile devices without managing servers, and CloudFront caches and delivers them close to users. Replicating files across Regions, Local Zone EC2 caches, or running your own EC2 converters adds cost and overhead.

Application Auto Scaling supports ECS services (including Fargate) with target tracking on CPU or memory, scaling tasks out and in automatically as utilization changes, which cuts costs when usage falls. EC2 Auto Scaling doesn't scale Fargate tasks, and a custom Lambda adds work.

AWS DataSync is a managed service that automates and accelerates transfers between NFS file systems (including across Regions) on a schedule, with minimal operational overhead. Snowball, a custom SFTP server, or DMS (for databases) aren't suited.

Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed service providing SMB file shares that Windows and compatible clients can mount. DataSync doesn't present a mountable file system, a self-managed Windows file share isn't fully managed, and S3 can't be mounted via SMB natively.

A cluster placement group in a single AZ gives the lowest latency and highest network throughput between instances and avoids inter-AZ data transfer charges. Partition placement across AZs and Auto Scaling across AZs add latency and data transfer costs.

A cached volume gateway stores the full dataset in S3 and keeps only recently accessed data in a local cache, which minimizes the need to scale on-premises iSCSI storage. Stored volumes keep all data locally, and tape and file gateways don't provide iSCSI block volumes.

Trusted Advisor checks are account-specific, so use the account where the RDS instances run, and review the Idle DB Instances check to find unused databases to reduce costs. The Reserved Instance Optimization check applies to instances running long term, but these run only 90 days, and the Redshift check is irrelevant.

S3 Storage Lens provides organization-wide activity metrics and dashboards, including advanced activity metrics that show which buckets are rarely or never accessed, with no setup of custom pipelines. The default console dashboard lacks this, and CloudWatch or CloudTrail analysis needs more work.

CloudFront with the S3 bucket as origin caches dataset files near customers in North America and Europe, reducing data transfer costs (CloudFront egress is cheaper than direct S3 egress) while maintaining or improving performance, and CloudFront signed URLs keep access control. Transfer Acceleration costs extra, and replicating buckets adds storage and transfer costs.

One SNS topic with SQS queues subscribed and message filtering by quote type delivers each quote type to its own durable queue, so quotes aren't lost and can be processed within 24 hours, with low maintenance. Kinesis streams, per-type Lambda/SNS, or OpenSearch searching add overhead or don't retain messages as simply.

AWS Backup can back up whole EC2 instances (configuration plus all attached EBS volumes) on a nightly schedule and copy the backups to another Region, with no custom code. Backing up only EBS volumes misses the instance configuration, and Lambda scripts are more work.
CloudFront delivers streaming content at global scale, and signed URLs restrict access to authorized users. A public bucket isn't restricted, and VPNs aren't practical for millions of mobile users.

Aurora Serverless for MySQL automatically scales capacity (and can pause when idle), so no instance type needs to be chosen, which fits infrequent access and future growth while remaining MySQL-compatible with minimal downtime. Aurora provisioned and RDS require choosing an instance class, and Redshift Spectrum is for querying S3.

Amazon Inspector scans EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure and produces findings reports, and Lambda can automate report distribution. Shield protects against DDoS, Macie finds sensitive data in S3, and GuardDuty detects threats rather than scanning for vulnerabilities.

Moving the polling script to Lambda, triggered by the SQS queue, scales automatically with message volume and you pay only for processing time, eliminating the always-on EC2 cost. A larger instance costs more, and the other options still require managing instances.

A scheduled AWS Glue ETL job reads the CSV files and loads them into Amazon Redshift, where the COTS application can run its SQL queries, with serverless ETL and low overhead. Custom EC2 scripts, DynamoDB (not supported by the COTS app), or EMR clusters add effort.

CloudTrail records who made which API calls (provisioning instances, changing security groups) for auditing, and AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes and evaluates them against rules for compliance. Lifecycle policies, Trusted Advisor, and CloudFormation restores don't audit changes.

Systems Manager Session Manager gives secure shell access using IAM permissions, with no SSH keys, no open inbound ports, and session logging, with low administrative overhead. STS can't generate SSH keys, and bastion hosts still use shared keys.

Kinesis Data Streams durably buffers the incoming JSON data so nothing is lost if an EC2 instance reboots, scales with ingestion rate, and Kinesis Data Analytics can query the stream in near real time with SQL. Instance store or EBS-based approaches can lose data, and Redshift via Firehose isn't as near-real-time.

A bucket policy that denies PutObject requests lacking the x-amz-server-side-encryption header ensures every uploaded object is encrypted. The ACL and SecureTransport conditions control access permissions and transport, not encryption at rest.

Placing a message on an SQS queue for thumbnail generation decouples the slow work from the upload, so the user can immediately be told the image was received while workers process the queue asynchronously. A synchronous Lambda or Step Functions workflow would still make the response wait for completion, and SNS doesn't buffer work.

API Gateway provides a highly available HTTPS endpoint, Lambda processes each message, and DynamoDB stores the results for the security team to analyze, all serverless. A single EC2 instance isn't highly available, Route 53 can't invoke Lambda directly, and a VPN design doesn't fit HTTPS sensors.

A stored volume gateway keeps the entire dataset locally (so users keep immediate, low-latency access to all files) over iSCSI, asynchronously backing it up to AWS as EBS snapshots for disaster recovery, with the least change to the existing infrastructure. A cached volume holds only part of the data locally, tape gateway isn't iSCSI file access, and File Gateway changes the protocol.

To access the protected S3 bucket, Cognito users need AWS credentials: the identity pool must assume an IAM role (authenticated role) that grants access to the protected bucket. The JWT from the user pool alone doesn't grant S3 permissions, and ACLs, redeployments, or attribute mappings don't solve it.
